title: TimeDistill: Efficient Long-Term Time Series Forecasting with MLP via Cross-Architecture Distillation

problem.claim: Transformer-based and CNN-based methods perform strongly in long-term time series forecasting but may be difficult to deploy at large scale because of high computational and storage requirements.

gap.claim: Lightweight MLP models need a way to benefit from the complementary multi-scale and multi-period patterns captured by advanced architectures.

contributions.claim: A cross-architecture knowledge distillation framework transfers temporal- and frequency-domain patterns from teacher models such as Transformers and CNNs to MLP.
A theoretical analysis interprets the knowledge-distillation approach as a specialized form of mixup data augmentation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: TimeDistill improves MLP performance by up to 18.6% and surpasses teacher models on eight datasets.
TimeDistill achieves up to 7X faster inference and requires 130X fewer parameters.
The authors report extensive evaluations highlighting the method's versatility and effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Transformer-based and CNN-based methods perform strongly in long-term time series forecasting.
Their computational and storage requirements can hinder large-scale deployment.
Different model architectures capture complementary multi-scale and multi-period patterns in temporal and frequency domains.
TimeDistill transfers these patterns from Transformer and CNN teachers to MLP through cross-architecture knowledge distillation.
The authors report improved MLP performance, faster inference, fewer parameters, and evaluations across multiple datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the eight datasets or baseline configurations.
